bodies.linkedin:
Farmers in 450 often abandoned their land to seek protection from local warlords, which deprived the empire of tax revenue.

The popular belief that the Roman Empire ended in a sudden, violent collapse is inaccurate. Before the events of 476, the Western Roman government faced internal instability, including an inability to pay its financial obligations.

Roman emperors devalued currency by mixing base metals into silver coins to cover rising military costs. This runaway inflation led merchants to reject imperial money in favor of trading grain and olive oil.

The vast physical size of the Roman Empire made it impossible for central armies to defend against fast-moving raiders. Local commanders often made private safety deals because central authority could not provide effective protection. The government suffered from internal rot as generals traded loyalty for bribes and engaged in frequent civil wars.

Rome did not vanish in a single dramatic afternoon.

The popular belief that the Roman Empire ended in a sudden, violent collapse is inaccurate. Rome did not vanish in a single dramatic afternoon.

The Western Roman government faced internal instability, including an inability to pay its financial obligations, before the events of 476.

Roman emperors devalued currency by mixing base metals into silver coins to cover rising military costs.

Runaway inflation caused by currency devaluation led merchants to reject imperial money in favor of trading grain and olive oil.

The vast physical size of the Roman Empire made it impossible for central armies to defend against fast-moving raiders.

Local commanders often made private safety deals because central authority could not provide effective protection.

The Roman government suffered from internal rot as generals traded loyalty for bribes and engaged in frequent civil wars.

Farmers in 450 often abandoned their land to seek protection from local warlords, which deprived the empire of tax revenue.

The fall of the Roman Empire was not a sudden event caused by external invasion, but a long process of internal systemic collapse.
